definitions.gloss: new construction; newly built structure or vessel
definitions.explanation: Refers to the building of something new, especially ships, buildings, or other large structures. Most commonly used in the context of shipbuilding to mean a newly constructed ship.
An older usage referring to a newly married woman or young wife. This sense is now archaic or dialectal but appears in classical literature and historical texts.

notes:
Primarily used in modern Japanese to refer to the construction of new ships, buildings, or large structures. The word carries a sense of building from scratch rather than renovating or modifying.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新造|しんぞう}⟦{船|せん}→船：09875_sen⟧: newly built ship
- ⟦{船|ふね}→船：00775_fune⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{新造|しんぞう}: construction of a new ship
- {新造|しんぞう}⟦{費|ひ}→費：09877_hi⟧: construction cost (for new build)
- {新造|しんぞう}⟦{車両|しゃりょう}→車両：05297_sharyou⟧: newly manufactured rolling stock

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{新築|しんちく}→新築：06567_shinchiku⟧: new construction (specifically buildings and houses)
- ⟦{建造|けんぞう}→建造：22998_kenzou⟧: construction (used for ships and large structures, emphasizes the building process)
- ⟦{造船|ぞうせん}→造船：04484_zousen⟧: shipbuilding (the industry or activity in general)

ETYMOLOGY:
In Edo-period usage, {新造|しんぞう} referred to a young woman, especially a newly married wife or a young woman working in the pleasure quarters. This sense survives in historical fiction and period dramas but is not used in modern everyday speech.
